key_insight: PyRUA-DataFarm explores using an LLM coding agent to replace repeated human teleoperation when creating robot demonstrations. Given a data request and one calibration episode, the agent rebuilds the task in simulation to generate additional data.
problem_solved: Robot demonstrations consume both operator and robot time, and collecting data for each new task often means starting over.
method: Provide the agent with a data request and one robot calibration episode from the target scene.
Have the agent write a simulated scene, an expert controller, and a success judge.
Use the simulator to supply exact actions; the provided abstract is truncated before explaining the video model's role.
impact: The approach could reduce the human effort and robot time needed to expand demonstration datasets. The supplied excerpt does not establish cost savings or real-world performance.
visual_elements: Pipeline: data request + calibration episode → coding agent → simulated task → demonstration data.
Three-part diagram showing the agent-built scene, expert controller, and success judge.
Side-by-side illustration of repeated human teleoperation versus agent-driven simulation.

paper_title: PyRUA-DataFarm: LLM Agent as a Cost-Efficient Teleoperator for Real-Ready Robot Data
paper_authors: Kewei Zhang, Juncheng Ma, Guodong Lv, Duomin Wang, Feixiang Ruan
